Petitioner in Kum.Mohitha.R., MVC 744/2022: D/o.Raghavendra, SCCH-9 2 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 Aged about 14 years, R/at No.455, III Stage, Kalpavrikshanagar, Kesare, Narasimharaja Mohalla, Mysore - 570007. By her mother & Natural Guardian Smt.Lakshmi.K., C.Krishna Murthy vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83064090/ 1 D/o.Krishna Murthy.C., Aged about 37 years. Petitioner in Kum.R.Nethravathi, MVC 745/2022: D/o.Raghavendra, Aged about 11 years, R/at No.455, III Stage, Kalpavrikshanagar, Kesare, Narasimharaja Mohalla, Mysore - 570007. Policy No.215700/31/ SCCH-9 3 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 2021/MI/249608 Valid from 18.03.2021 to 17.03.2022 (By Sri. R.S.Srikanta Reddy -Adv.) 2. (Exparte) // COMMON JUDGMENT // These petitions are filed by the petitioners against the C.Krishna Murthy vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83064090/ 2 respondents claiming compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act for the injuries sustained by them in RTA. 2.
texts.facts: C.Krishna Murthy vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83064090/ 3 X-rays were taken, which revealed fracture injuries. The petitioners have violated the provisions of Motor vehicles Act by triple riding. The accident was caused sole negligence of Car driver and petitioners have sustained injuries.
texts.arguments: Hence, I am of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.60,000/- . There is no physical disability to the petitioner to the accidental injury. Therefore, there is no question of awarding compensation for loss of future earnings. The petitioner has not examined the doctor and also not produced any disability certificate to show that she is suffering from physical disability. Therefore, in view of non production of disability certificate and doctor evidence regarding disability, it cannot be considered as the petitioner is having physical disability due to the accidental injury. There is no dispute about medical bills. There is no physical disability to the petitioner to the accidental injury. Therefore, there is no question of awarding compensation for loss of future earnings. Therefore, by considering the injuries sustained, treatment taken and medical bills produced by the petitioner, it is just and proper to award the Global Compensation. Hence, I am of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.1,30,000/- 22. The Respondent No.2 also SCCH-9 23 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 C.Krishna Murthy vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83064090/ 17 contended that the petitioners have contributed their negligence for occurring the accident. In this regard he has relied upon the following reported judgments: 1) 2004 (1) KLJ 498 (P.S.Somaiah & anr V/s C.Krishna Murthy vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83064090/ 18 The Director, Bangalore Dairy and Others), wherein it is observed that - If any rider of Motor cycle violates Sec.128 of M.V.Act moving in a triple riding then contributory negligence to be considered and compensation should be apportioned on the apportionment of negligence. 2) 2003 (2) TAC 103 (Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Coimbatore Dvn) Ltd., Coimbatore V/s Abdul Salam & Others), wherein Hon'ble Madras High Court observed that riding the motor cycle more than seating capacity amounts to a negligence and contributory negligence be considered while awarding the compensation in accident case. 3) 2017 ACJ 418 (New India Assurance Co.., Ltd., V/s Hemanth & Others), wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that- in case of triple riding there is a contributory negligence and SCCH-9 25 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 liability to be fixed on apportionment to the insurance companies.
